subject: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors

messages.author: 167ba54486295fa6
messages.subject: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors
parts:
Hi All,
I was wondering about the behaviour of the choices option in selectInput. if I pass in choices=x where x is

x= c("a","a","b","b","c")
name(x) = 1:length(x)

the names 1:5 are shown in the selectInput and the selected value is returned. Given that in the above case the values are not unique it is impossible to know which one was selected. Furthermore why would the indices be presented and not the actual values of the vector. What was the reasoning to choose this behaviour and how would I solve a case with non unique choices but the position in the data.frame or vector is desired?

Regards

Christoph

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors
parts:
Labels are for users to read and choose from, and values are for app
authors (e.g. you). Users probably don't care about values, and
authors don't care about labels. It is totally your choice to use
unique values or not. If you want to know exactly which choice the
user selected, you have to use unique values.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 167ba54486295fa6
messages.subject: Re: selectInput choices presents naes of vectors
parts:
OK, my point is if users and authors don't care, why not swap it around? Use values as labels and names as reactive return values. That would make it possible to have non unique values and know exactly where they are coming from. Of course if you just swap it, would break all other applications but adding a variable which can be set to true to swap it would not. This would give the developer the freedom of choice.

Christoph
